source_refs.note: Exercise 1.5, Question 12 (book page 33); answers PDF 301 (book page 299)

blocks.prompt: 12 An amount of Rs. 2000 becomes 3320.12 under continuous compounding at 6% per annum. Find the time \(t\).
blocks.explanation:
A continuous compound interest question in reverse: the time is unknown.
\(t\) is in the exponent of \(e^{0.06t}\).
Plan: substitute, divide by 2000, take \(\ln\), divide by 0.06.
steps:
Given: \(P = 2000\), \(A = 3320.12\), \(r = 0.06\).
To find: the time \(t\) (years).
Method: \(A = Pe^{rt}\); isolate \(e^{0.06t}\) and take \(\ln\).

Substitute the values
\[3320.12 = 2000e^{0.06t}\]
Why: continuous compounding model with the known values.

Make the exponential stand alone
\[e^{0.06t} = \dfrac{3320.12}{2000}\]
\[= 1.66006\]
Why: divide by 2000.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key prints \(t \approx 8.42\) years. With \(t = 8.42\) the amount would be \(2000e^{0.06 \times 8.42} \approx\) Rs. 3314.63, not Rs. 3320.12. The correct value is \(t = \frac{\ln 1.66006}{0.06} \approx 8.45\) years.
